Balancing the credit

The broken rule frames the credit symmetrically, which shows how unbalanced the line inside it is. These six rebuild the line around its centre, and all of them cut it down to one typeface for the words and one accent for the rule. Captured from the running drawer, actual size.

ABroken rule on today’s line
Your pick, as the line stands now. The frame is symmetric; what sits inside it is not. A wide grey label on the left, two bright marks on the right, and five treatments in between.
BOne typeface, one line
Label and name both in Vollkorn italic, so it reads as a phrase. The section mark and dotted underline go. Still weighted to the right, where the marks are.
CTwo lines, marks centred below
The phrase sits on the rule; the marks drop to their own centred line. Balanced, but taller, and it pushes the buttons down.
DMarks as the ends of the rule
The two marks flank the name and become the rule’s end caps. The small label sits above, centred. Symmetric about the name on both lines.
Recommended
EMarks as the ends, no label
D without the label. The cleanest and most balanced, and it relies on its position under the portrait to say it is a credit.
FThree centred lines
Label, name on the rule, marks below. Formal, like a plate, and the tallest of the six.
